questions.question: A new agent opens Incident > All and sees rows and columns of incident data. How should they interpret this screen?

options.text: A form showing one incident record and its fields
A list of incident records, with one field per column
A report of incident counts, with one group per column
A view definition, with one form section per column

explanation.correct: This screen is a list. ServiceNow documentation describes a list as displaying a set of records from a table, and states that each column in a list corresponds to a field on the table, so each row the agent sees is one incident record and each column is one Incident field. Users can search, sort, filter, and edit data directly in the list. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UseLists.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A form displays information from one record in a table. Seeing many incident rows at once means this is a list, not the form of a single record.
Counting records per group is what a grouped list or a report does. A plain list shows the individual records, one per row, rather than aggregated counts.
A view defines which elements appear when a list or form opens, but it is not shown as a grid of form sections; the columns here are table fields.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: A list shows records from a table. On the ServiceNow platform, lists can be interacted with in various ways. In both the core platform and workspace, each row is a record and each column is a field.

questions.question: What is the purpose of views in ServiceNow?

options.text: To delete records from the database
To display lists or forms in different ways for different user types
To create new tables automatically
To import data from external sources

explanation.correct: Views allow users to display lists or forms in different ways. System administrators can create views for different user types, such as employee, self-service, and mobile users. The number of records stays the same, but field order may vary. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Views don't delete records; they only control how data is displayed.
Table creation is a separate administrative function.
Data import is handled by Import Sets, not views.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Views allow users to display lists or forms in different ways. System administrators can create views for different user types, such as employee, self-service, and mobile users.

questions.question: What is dot-walking in ServiceNow?

options.text: A method to delete multiple records at once
Collecting data from related tables via reference fields
A type of user authentication
A workflow execution pattern

explanation.correct: Dot-walking collects data from related tables via reference fields. It works in form layout, but not in form design. It's commonly used in form builder, list views, platform analytics, and Workflow Studio. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Deleting records is done through list editing or bulk delete, not dot-walking.
Authentication is managed separately and unrelated to dot-walking.
Workflow execution follows different patterns; dot-walking is about data relationships.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Dot-walking collects data from related tables via reference fields. It works in form layout, but not in form design.

questions.question: What are the three parts of a filter condition in ServiceNow?

options.text: Table, Record, and Value
Field, Operator, and Value
User, Role, and Permission
Name, Description, and Category

explanation.correct: A filter condition has three parts: Field (can include related tables), Operator (varies by field type, like 'greater than' for numbers), and Value (text entry or choice list based on field type). See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: While tables and records are concepts in ServiceNow, they're not the three parts of a filter condition.
User, Role, and Permission relate to security, not filter conditions.
These are common field types but not the components of a filter condition.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: A filter condition has three parts. Field-- able to be chosen based on user access, can include related tables. Operator-- varies by field type. Value-- text entry or choice list based on field.

questions.question: An agent wants the Business service column on their own Incident list, but their teammates' lists must stay exactly as they are. What should the agent use?

options.text: Configure > List Layout from a column heading
The personalize list icon to choose their columns
A new list view created from the List Layout slushbucket
A Group By on the Business service column heading

explanation.correct: Personal lists let a user choose which columns appear and in what order for a specific list view, based on individual preferences. ServiceNow documentation states that personal list customizations do not affect what other users see, and the agent opens them with the personalize list icon in the corner of the list. This meets the goal without changing the shared layout. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_PersonalLists.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Configure > List Layout changes the columns of the list view itself, the layout every user of that view receives, so teammates would also see the new column.
Creating views requires the admin role and is done from List Layout, so it is not an agent's personal setting. A view is a named layout other users can switch to, not a personal preference.
Group By aggregates the list by a field and shows a record count per group. It organizes records but does not add a column to the list.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Where the list layout configuration affects everyone, the personalize list modifies the layout of a list for an individual user. It does not affect the platform default.

questions.question: A user has personalized their incident list view. Later, an administrator adds a new column to the default list view. What will happen for that user?

options.text: The user will automatically see the new column
The user will not see the new column until they choose 'reset to column defaults'
The user's personalization will be automatically deleted
The administrator's change will be rejected

explanation.correct: Any global changes that occur at the system level will not be reflected in a personalized list. If the system administrator configures a list view a user has personalized, they will not see those newly added default changes until they choose reset to column defaults. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Personalization overrides system defaults; users must manually reset to see new default columns.
User personalization is preserved; it just overrides the system view.
Admin changes are applied to the system default, they just don't override user personalizations.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Any global changes that occur at the system level will not be reflected in a personalized list. If the system administrator configures a list view a user has personalized, they will not see those newly added default changes until they choose reset to column defaults.

questions.question: Where is the view name displayed on a list or form?

options.text: At the bottom of the page
In brackets beside the table or form title (unless it's the default view)
In the Application Navigator
In the user profile settings

explanation.correct: The view name will appear in brackets beside the table or form title, unless it's the default view. This helps users identify which view they are currently using. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: View names are displayed near the title, not at the bottom of the page.
The Application Navigator shows modules and menus, not current view names.
User profile settings contain user preferences, not current view indicators.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

questions.question: An agent selects an incident number in the Incident list, and a page opens showing fields, form sections, and related lists for that incident. What is this page?

options.text: A list showing records from several related tables
A form showing the data of that incident record
A report summarizing that incident's field values
A dashboard showing the Incident table's settings

explanation.correct: The page is a form. ServiceNow documentation states that a form displays information from one record in a data table, and that users can view and edit records in forms. Fields, sections, and related lists are all listed as form elements; the related lists only show records from other tables that relate to this one incident. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UsingForms.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Although related lists appear at the bottom of the form, the page itself presents one incident record. A list is the view that shows a set of records from a table.
Forms are not reports that summarize data: the documentation says users can view and edit records in forms, and they save changes with Submit, Update, or Save.
The form displays data stored in the selected record, not table configuration. Administrators change the form's contents through form configuration, not by viewing a record.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Forms in ServiceNow show information from a single record in a table, and can be accessed through global search or lists.

questions.question: Which elements are included on ServiceNow forms? (Choose two)

options.text: Fields and sections
Import sets
Related lists
Scheduled jobs

explanation.correct: Forms include fields, sections, formatters, UI actions, and related lists. These elements enhance how users navigate and interact with forms. Import sets and scheduled jobs are separate functionalities. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Import sets are for data loading, not form elements.
Scheduled jobs run automated tasks, they're not form components.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

questions.question: An agent edits several fields on an incident form and then opens a different module without saving. The instance uses default form settings. What happens?

options.text: The changes are saved automatically as a draft
A message asks them to confirm leaving the page
The changes are discarded with no message shown
The form locks editing until the record is saved

explanation.correct: Navigating away from a form without saving is how a user cancels changes. ServiceNow documentation says that when a confirmation message appears, the user selects Leave this Page to confirm the cancellation, and that administrators can turn this message off by setting glide.ui.dirty_form_support to false. With default settings, the agent is warned before the unsaved edits are lost. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_EditingInForms.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Changes are kept only when the record is saved with Submit, Update, or Save. Navigating away without saving cancels the changes; it does not store a draft.
The changes are discarded only after the user confirms. The silent behavior happens only if an administrator disables the message with glide.ui.dirty_form_support.
Nothing in the documented form editing behavior locks the record. The user either confirms leaving the page or stays on the form to keep editing and save.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

questions.question: What are the three ways to modify a form in ServiceNow?

options.text: Import, Export, and Copy
Form Builder, Form Design, and Form Layout
Create, Update, and Delete
View, Edit, and Preview

explanation.correct: There are several ways to modify a form: Form Builder, Form Design, and Form Layout. Each provides different capabilities for form customization. Administrators should avoid adding the same editable field in multiple sections. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Import, Export, and Copy are data operations, not form modification methods.
These are CRUD operations on records, not form configuration tools.
These describe user interactions, not form modification methods.

questions.question: Service desk agents type the same category, subcategory, and assignment group on every password reset incident. An administrator wants them to fill these fields in one step. What should the administrator provide?

options.text: A new table that extends Incident for resets
A form template storing those field values
A list view filtered to reset incidents
A scheduled report of past reset incidents

explanation.correct: Form templates exist to simplify submitting new records by populating fields automatically. The documented approach is to fill in the most-used fields for a table, save them as a template, and make the template available to users, who can then apply it when creating a record (for example from the template bar). See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_Templates.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Extending the Incident table creates a new table structure; it does not supply default values for the fields agents fill in on each new incident.
A list view controls which fields appear when the list opens. It helps agents find existing records but does not prefill fields on a new one.
Reports summarize and display existing data. A scheduled report of past incidents gives no way to populate fields on a record being created.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: To use a template, fill in the most common fields for a table. Save it as a template, and make it available to users. Users can apply templates manually when creating records, or administrators can set scripts to apply them automatically.

questions.question: Why should only certain groups be allowed to create templates?

options.text: To reduce system storage usage
To avoid bypassing processes like mandatory fields and UI policies
To prevent users from seeing each other's data
To improve system performance

explanation.correct: Only certain groups should create templates to avoid bypassing processes, like mandatory fields and UI policies, particularly for records using condition based flows or workflows. Templates can potentially skip validation rules if not properly controlled. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Storage is not the primary concern with template creation.
Data visibility is controlled by ACLs, not template permissions.
System performance is not significantly impacted by template creation.

questions.question: What happens when a user personalizes a form using the personalize form feature?

options.text: The changes affect all users on the platform
The personalized form will remain each time the user logs in
Mandatory fields can be hidden
The changes are temporary and reset on logout

explanation.correct: The personalized form will remain each time the user logs in. Only fields configured to display are available in the personalize form menu. Mandatory fields cannot be hidden through personalization. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Personalization only affects the individual user, not all users.
Mandatory fields cannot be hidden through the personalize form feature.
Personalization persists across sessions for the user.

questions.question: In Form Builder, which elements can administrators configure in the policies and rules section? (Choose two)

options.text: UI policies
Database schemas
Business rules
Network settings

explanation.correct: In the Form Builder policies and rules section, administrators can configure UI policies, access control rules, client scripts, business rules, and workspace view rules. Database schemas and network settings are managed elsewhere. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Database schemas are managed through table configuration, not Form Builder.
Network settings are system-level configurations, not form-related.

questions.question: What is the purpose of dot-walking in ServiceNow?

options.text: To navigate between application menus
To access fields from related tables through reference fields
To create new database tables
To configure user roles and permissions

explanation.correct: Dot-walking collects data from related tables via reference fields. It allows you to access fields on referenced records, commonly used in form builder, form layout, list views, platform analytics, and Workflow Studio.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dot-walking is about accessing data across related tables, not navigating menus.
Table creation is done through System Definition > Tables, not dot-walking.
Role configuration is done through User Administration, not dot-walking.

questions.question: What happens when a system administrator configures a list view that a user has already personalized?

options.text: The user's personalized view is automatically updated with the new changes
The user will NOT see the new default changes until they choose 'Reset to column defaults'
The personalized view is deleted and replaced with the new configuration
Both views are merged automatically

explanation.correct: Any global changes at the system level will not be reflected in a personalized list. The user must choose 'Reset to column defaults' to see newly added default changes.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Personalized views are independent of system-level changes and are not automatically updated.
Personalized views persist until the user explicitly resets them.
There is no automatic merging of personalized and system views.

questions.question: Which of the following are ways to modify a form in ServiceNow? (Choose 3)

options.text: Form Builder
Form Design
Form Layout
Form Schema

explanation.correct: There are three ways to modify a form in ServiceNow: Form Builder, Form Design, and Form Layout. Form Schema is not a valid form modification tool.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Form Schema is not a form modification method. Schema Map is used for viewing table relationships, not form editing.

questions.question: A user wants to hide certain fields on a form without affecting other users. Which feature should they use?

options.text: Form Builder
Form Layout
Personalize Form
UI Policy

explanation.correct: Personalize Form allows individual users to hide fields on a form without affecting other users. The personalized form remains each time the user logs in. Mandatory fields cannot be hidden.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Form Builder modifies the form for all users, not just the individual.
Form Layout changes affect all users viewing that form.
UI Policies can hide fields but affect all users matching the conditions, not just individual personalization.

questions.question: Which statement about the List Editor is correct?

options.text: It allows editing only one record at a time
It is the quickest method to update a field on multiple records
It overrides all security constraints
It is enabled for all tables by default

explanation.correct: The List Editor is the quickest method to update a field on multiple records, supporting both contiguous and noncontiguous editing. If a row cannot be edited due to security constraints, a message is displayed.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The List Editor supports editing multiple records simultaneously.
Security constraints still apply — if a row can't be edited, a message indicates the field cannot be edited.
By default, list editing is disabled or restricted for some tables.

questions.question: In Form Builder, how do you add a dot-walked field from a related table to a form?

options.text: Right-click the form and select 'Add Related Field'
Select 'Add a Related Field' under the desired field, then drag it to the form
Navigate to System Definition > Tables and add the field there
Use the Schema Map to drag fields between tables

explanation.correct: In Form Builder, to dot walk, select 'Add a Related Field' under the desired field, then drag it to the form. In the Dot Walk window, select a field from the table or navigate to a related table, then click Add to View.

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no right-click option for adding related fields in Form Builder.
System Definition > Tables is for table management, not for adding dot-walked fields to forms.
Schema Map is for visualizing relationships, not for adding fields to forms.

questions.question: A user reports that a reference field on a form is not displaying the expected records in its dropdown. Which two actions should an administrator investigate? (Choose 2)

options.text: The reference qualifier on the field restricts which records appear
The form view is set to mobile layout
The user lacks read access to the referenced table
The field label has been changed recently

explanation.correct: Reference qualifiers filter which records appear in a reference field dropdown. Additionally, if the user doesn't have read access to the referenced table, records won't appear. Both conditions should be checked when troubleshooting missing reference field records.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Mobile layout affects form appearance but doesn't filter reference field records.
Changing a field label doesn't affect which records appear in the dropdown.

questions.question: Which statement about Next Experience UI is NOT true?

options.text: It uses the Polaris theme by default
It replaces UI16 as the default interface for all users
The Unified Navigation framework supports configurable menus
Workspaces can be accessed from the All menu

wrongAnswers.explanation: Next Experience does use the Polaris theme as its default visual design.
Unified Navigation does support configurable menus and navigation.
Workspaces are accessible through the All menu in Next Experience.

questions.question: In the List v3 component, what happens when an administrator configures a 'condition' on a list?

options.text: It permanently deletes records that don't match
It applies a filter that restricts which records are displayed
It changes the table schema
It creates a new view of the table

explanation.correct: A condition on a list component acts as a filter, restricting which records from the table are displayed. It does not modify data or create new views.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Conditions filter the display; they never delete records.
List conditions don't modify the table schema.
A condition filters within the current view, it doesn't create a new view.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: An administrator needs to ensure that a specific form layout appears only when the Priority field is set to 1 - Critical. Which feature should they use?

options.text: Form views with a view rule
UI Policy to hide fields
ACL on the form
Client script to redirect

explanation.correct: View rules allow administrators to automatically switch form views based on conditions like field values. Setting a view rule on the Priority field being Critical will display the specific form layout.

wrongAnswers.explanation: UI Policies can show/hide individual fields but don't switch entire form layouts.
ACLs control access permissions, not form layout presentation.
Client scripts for redirection are not the standard approach for conditional form layouts.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: Which statements about ServiceNow list editing are true? (Choose 2)

options.text: Double-clicking a cell in a list enables inline editing for that field
List editing allows updating multiple records simultaneously using the list header checkbox
All field types support inline list editing without restrictions
List editing must be enabled by a system property before it can be used

explanation.correct: Double-clicking a cell enables inline editing, and selecting multiple records via the header checkbox allows bulk updates. Both are core list editing capabilities in ServiceNow.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Some field types like Journal fields and encrypted fields do not support inline list editing.
List editing is enabled by default in ServiceNow, though it can be disabled by administrators.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Favorites' feature in ServiceNow navigation?

options.text: It bookmarks specific records or modules for quick access from the navigation bar
It automatically prioritizes frequently used tables
It creates shortcuts to external websites
It pins dashboards to the homepage

explanation.correct: Favorites allow users to bookmark specific records, lists with filters, or application modules for quick access from the favorites icon in the navigation bar.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Favorites are manually set by users, not automatically determined by usage frequency.
Favorites are for internal ServiceNow navigation, not external websites.
Dashboard pinning is separate from the Favorites feature.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: A user needs to see incidents assigned to their group AND with a state of 'In Progress'. Which filter operation should be used?

options.text: Use OR condition between Assignment Group and State
Use AND condition between Assignment Group and State
Create two separate filtered lists and compare them
Use a CONTAINS condition on both fields

explanation.correct: When both conditions must be true simultaneously (assigned to their group AND in progress), an AND condition is required. This returns only records matching both criteria.

wrongAnswers.explanation: OR would return records matching either condition, not both — showing incidents from other groups or in other states.
Creating separate lists is unnecessary; the filter builder supports multiple conditions natively.
CONTAINS is for text matching within a field value, not for filtering by exact field values like group or state.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: An administrator wants a shorter Incident form that shows only a few metrics fields, while agents keep the Default form unchanged. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create a new view and use Form Layout to pick its fields
Remove the extra fields from the Default view in Form Layout
Use the personalize list icon to hide the extra fields
Add a form section and collapse it for other users

explanation.correct: A view defines the elements that appear when a user opens a form or list, so a separate view can show a smaller subset of fields while the Default view stays the same. Administrators create a view from Configure > Form Layout by basing it on an existing view and then choosing the fields for that view. The documentation even uses the Incident form shown in a Metrics view as an example. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/view-management-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Editing the Default view in Form Layout changes the form every user of that view sees, so the agents' Default form would lose those fields as well.
The personalize list icon changes one user's column choices on a list. It does not configure which fields appear on the Incident form for a group of users.
Sections group fields, but collapsing a section is saved as each user's own preference, so an administrator cannot use it to define a shorter form for others.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: What enables collecting data from related tables via reference fields in ServiceNow?

options.text: Field mapping
Dot-walking
Table joins
Reference linking

explanation.correct: Dot-walking is ServiceNow's method for accessing data from related tables through reference fields. When you have a reference field pointing to another table, you can 'walk' through the reference using dot notation to access fields in the referenced table. For example, if an incident has a 'caller_id' reference field pointing to the user table, you can access the caller's department using 'caller_id.department'. This is fundamental to ServiceNow's data access patterns and is used extensively in both the UI and scripting.

references.title: ServiceNow Administration Fundamentals - Lists and Filters

questions.question: A service desk manager wants the Incident list organized by Assignment group, with a record count shown for each group. What should they do from the list's column heading?

options.text: Right-click the column and select Sort (a to z)
Right-click the column name and select Group By
Right-click and select Configure > List Layout
Right-click a value and select Show Matching

explanation.correct: Grouping aggregates a list by a field and displays the record count per group. ServiceNow documentation lists right-clicking the column name and selecting Group By as one way to group a list (Ungroup removes it). Each group is named after a field value, here an assignment group, and the count appears next to the group name. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_GroupedLists.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Sort (a to z) orders the records by that column in ascending order. The records stay in one list and no per-group record counts are shown.
Configure > List Layout changes which columns appear in the list view and their order. It does not aggregate records or show counts per group.
Show Matching is a quick filter that limits the list to records with the selected value. It narrows the list to one group instead of organizing all of them.

questions.question: A user sees brackets around a list view name like '[Assigned to me]'. What does this indicate?

options.text: The view is locked by an administrator
The view is currently being edited
The view is not the default list view
The view has active filters applied

explanation.correct: Brackets around a list view name indicate that you are not viewing the default list view. ServiceNow shows brackets to make it clear when you've switched from the default view to a different saved view, such as 'Assigned to me', 'Recent', or custom views. The default view typically shows without brackets. This visual indicator helps users understand which view they're currently using and is important for navigation awareness.

references.title: ServiceNow Administration Fundamentals - Lists and Filters

questions.question: Which methods can be used to modify form layouts in ServiceNow? (Choose 2)

options.text: Form Designer
List Editor
Form Layout Tool
UI Policy Designer

explanation.correct: ServiceNow provides two primary methods for modifying form layouts: Form Designer (a drag-and-drop interface for arranging form elements) and Form Layout Tool (for more advanced layout modifications). List Editor is used for customizing list views, not forms. UI Policy Designer creates dynamic form behaviors but doesn't directly modify layouts. Understanding the distinction between these tools is important for form customization tasks.

references.title: ServiceNow Administration Fundamentals - Forms and Configuration

questions.question: An agent sees the breadcrumbs All > Active = true > Category = Software > Priority = 2 on the Incident list and wants to drop only the Category condition. What should they select?

options.text: The Category = Software breadcrumb
The separator (>) before Category = Software
The All breadcrumb at the start of the trail
The Priority = 2 breadcrumb at the end

explanation.correct: Breadcrumbs show the current filter as a hierarchy, from the most general condition on the left to the most specific on the right. According to ServiceNow documentation, selecting the condition separator (>) before a condition removes only that condition, so the list keeps Active = true and Priority = 2 and drops Category = Software. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UsingFiltersAndBreadcrumbs.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Selecting a breadcrumb removes every condition to its right. Choosing Category = Software would drop Priority = 2 and keep the Category condition.
Selecting All removes every condition and returns all incidents in the system, so the Active and Priority conditions would also be lost.
Priority = 2 is the last breadcrumb, so nothing sits to its right; selecting it only refreshes the list and leaves the Category condition in place.

questions.question: Which list personalization options are available to users in ServiceNow? (Choose 3)

options.text: Rearrange column order
Set column widths
Create new table fields
Save custom list views
Modify table schemas

explanation.correct: Users can personalize lists by rearranging column order (dragging columns to preferred positions), setting column widths (adjusting the display width of columns), and saving custom list views (preserving filter and display preferences). Users cannot create new table fields or modify table schemas - these are administrative functions requiring proper roles and permissions. List personalization focuses on display and organization, not data structure modifications.

references.title: ServiceNow Administration Fundamentals - Lists and Filters

questions.question:
Evaluate these statements about ServiceNow configuration:
A) Personal list configurations only affect the current user's view
B) System-level form modifications affect all users
C) Related lists show records from the same table as the main form

options.text: A and B are true, C is false
A and C are true, B is false
B and C are true, A is false
All statements are true

explanation.correct: Statement A is TRUE: Personal list configurations (column order, widths, personal views) only affect the individual user's experience. Statement B is TRUE: System-level form modifications (adding fields, changing layouts, UI policies) affect all users unless overridden by role-based configurations. Statement C is FALSE: Related lists typically show records from different tables that are related to the current record via reference fields (e.g., incidents related to a CI, tasks related to a change).

references.title: ServiceNow Administration Fundamentals - Forms and Lists Configuration

questions.question: An administrator adds items to a related list using a list collector (slushbucket). Which of the following is NOT a feature of the list collector interface?

options.text: An Available column listing items that can be added
A Selected column listing items already chosen
Add and remove icons that move items between columns
A drag-and-drop canvas for placing fields on a form

explanation.correct: The documented list collector interface has two columns, available items on the left and selected items on the right, with add (>) and remove (<) icons, double-click to move items, and in some cases search, filter, and up/down ordering controls. A drag-and-drop canvas for placing fields on a form is not part of it; that kind of visual layout belongs to form design tools. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_UseSlushbuckets.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The documentation states that the list collector shows the available items in a column on the left, from which the administrator picks items to add.
The selected items appear in the right-hand column, and new items are added to the bottom of that column, so this is a standard part of the interface.
Items move with the add icon (>) and the remove icon (<), or by double-clicking, so these icons are a documented list collector feature.
